summary: Tenant event handoff: incremental watermarks, HMAC anchors, and pseudonymized field mapping for third‑party SIEM
description: Issue summary: Customer requests a daily incremental handoff of tenant-scoped audit events to their SIEM vendor with per-file HMAC anchors, resume tokens, and a field-level pseudonymization mapping for PHI-sensitive fields. Impact: Medoria ingests Redwood audit events into a regulated analytics pipeline; missing cryptographic anchors and inconsistent redaction mappings block their legal team from accepting the feed. Request: 1) Signed manifest per export containing SHA256 checksums and HMAC anchor using a customer-provided KEK; 2) Per-record pseudonymization for specified fields (user.email, user.phone, payment.card_last4) with reversible token mapping held by customer; 3) Resume token in each file for deterministic replay; 4) UTC canonicalization of timestamps and consistent timezone normalization; 5) Delivery via S3 with server-side encryption and lifecycle 365d. Desired acceptance criteria: artifacts include manifest.json, data-part-00000.ndjson.gz, resume.token, and hmac.anchor; all checksums and HMACs validate against the KEK and field mappings match the provided specification.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer configured tenant export in Console → Integrations → Audit Exports with destination s3://medoria-redwood-exports/prod/
2) Selected 'incremental daily' and uploaded KEK public key for HMAC anchors
3) Expected files to include manifest.json + hmac.anchor + resume.token. Actual: data files present, manifest.json missing 'hmac_anchor' field, some timestamp fields in local tz, and user.email appears unhashed for a small subset (approx 0.2%).

investigation_notes: Initial triage by SRE (Miguel): reproduced export for tenant medoria-prod. Observed manifest.json schema v2 produced by exporter includes 'checksums' and 'timestamp' but 'hmac_anchor' field is only present if keystore alias matches internal naming convention. Customer uploaded KEK with alias 'medoria-kev-2026' while exporter expected pattern 'tenant-{tenant_id}-export-kek' causing conditional skip. Further, small percentage of records had 'user.email' emitting plaintext due to a race in the pseudonymization pipeline when the token cache miss path fell back to passthrough; high concurrency at time of run (~500 parallel writes) surfaced the bug. Hypothesis: conditional keystore lookup plus race in tokenization cache leads to missing HMAC and sporadic unhashed fields. Next steps: 1) Offer immediate workaround to regenerate artifacts with a temporary internal HMAC anchor signed by Redwood-approved service (customer consent obtained); 2) Patch exporter to accept arbitrary KEK aliases and fall back to provided public key; 3) Fix tokenization cache race (PR drafted).

SRE (2026-03-12) - Miguel: Created hotfix branch to accept explicit public key and to harden tokenization cache; running CI and internal export test. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287
Support (2026-03-12) - Aisha: Provided instructions for validating anchor when we upload signed_hmac_anchor.tar.gz to S3. Awaiting acceptance testing from Medoria.

Customer (Medoria Security, 2026-03-12) - Elena Park: Downloaded artifacts and validated checksums. HMAC anchor validated against Redwood attestation. Noted one remaining timestamp in data-part-00000 had 'America/Chicago' tz — requesting canonicalization sweep for that file.
resolution: Workaround applied: Redwood produced signed hmac_anchor using internal attestation key and uploaded signed_hmac_anchor.tar.gz to customer's S3 path per their DPA. Customer accepted temporary artifact on 2026-03-12 after validation. Long-term fix: exporter patched to accept explicit KEK public key regardless of alias and to canonicalize timestamps to UTC during export; tokenization cache race fix merged in PR#1287. Release plan: staged rollout to prod exports on 2026-03-17 (canary tenants 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Post-deployment actions: run a backfill for medoria for exports 2026-03-01..2026-03-09 with canonicalization and reissued hmac anchors; generate confluence postmortem and send SOC evidence bundle to Medoria security. Follow-up owner: Miguel Ortega.
